title: Ephemeral pulse failover coordinator and SLO anchoring
author: Maya Ortiz
release_notes: Introduce ephemeral pulse failover coordinator to reduce noisy tenant evictions during short regional blips; adds SLO anchoring to protect tenant capacity during transient failures.
description: Summary: Introduces a lightweight Ephemeral Pulse Failover Coordinator that emits short periodic probes (pulses) to detect transient regional egress blips and orchestrate soft handoffs for tenant traffic while anchoring minimum SLO capacity. Motivation: recent incidents showed that sticky circuit closures during sub-minute regional noise caused cascading tenant evictions and oscillation; we need a middle path that avoids aggressive eviction while keeping overall SLOs intact. High-level changes: 1) coord/pulse_coordinator.go: new coordinator implementing pulse probes, ephemeral reservation tokens, and an adaptive retry window. 2) coord/anchor_service.go: SLO anchoring layer which pins a minimal token budget per tenant during a pulse window to prevent starvation. 3) runtime/conn_manager.go: soft drain refactor and prioritized handoff logic with smoother exponential backoff to avoid hot loops. 4) telemetry/metrics.go: new metrics and sampling hooks (metrics.slo_pulse, metrics.pulse_sample_rate) and tracing tags for pulse lifecycle. 5) cfg/features.yaml: feature flag 'ephemeral_pulse_enabled' and rollout percentages. 6) integrations/staging-canary.yml: canary job wiring. 7) tests/pulse_coordinator_test.go: unit and integration tests including race scenarios. Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2389); [x] Unit tests added; [x] Integration/staging canary executed; [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated; [x] Security review completed. Commits (summary): - Add pulse coordinator implementation and public interface - Implement SLO anchor service and token semantics - Refactor conn_manager soft drain path to support ephemeral tokens - Add telemetry + sampling strategy - Add config toggles and canary workflow - Fix race in conn_manager found during tests Review conversation: Ethan Zhao: "Design looks sound, please document token expiry semantics and add a unit test covering race with conn_manager." Maya Ortiz (author): "Added inline docs and a deterministic unit test that reproduces and validates the race handling; adjusted expiry granularity to 500ms windows." Priya Kapoor: "Telemetry event cardinality is a risk at high QPS; suggest sampling or tag-based reduction." Maya Ortiz: "Added stratified sampling to metrics.slo_pulse (default 1/1000) and made it configurable per-tenant; added aggregate counters for observability." Luca Romano: "LGTM pending CI green; focusing on long-run stability." CI summary: Build: pass; Unit tests: pass (1185 tests, all green); Integration tests: pass; Lint: pass; Load tests: initial run had transient timing failure in conn_manager test, rerun passed; Staging canary: ran for 2h at 5% traffic, observed 0.6% reduction in 99P tail for affected endpoints and no SLO regressions. Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-20 into main. Rollout plan: feature flag off by default; staged rollout: 5% for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> 100% if no regressions. Monitoring: alerts under ENG-2390 created to track pulse_miss_rate, slo_anchor_utilization, and tenant_starvation_events. Rollback: disable 'ephemeral_pulse_enabled' and run documented drain script to revoke ephemeral tokens; hotfix steps documented in ENG-2390. Impact and compatibility: No breaking public API changes; config additions are backward compatible. Operations notes: sampling default tuned to limit high-cardinality events; support runbook updated. Security: no new network surface; token semantics validated by security review. Related work: builds on earlier soft-drain and circuit smoothing efforts but introduces short-lived reservation windows to avoid unnecessary long-term evictions. Follow-ups: (a) telemetry per-region heatmap, (b) admin UI toggle for manual quarantine and token introspection, (c) evaluate heuristics for adaptive sample rates at very high QPS.
